cases.description: Real cue: 'as it deems necessary'. The actor named in the cue is the pronoun 'it', which must resolve back to the sentence's own main actor ('the board') rather than being left as a bare pronoun. 'Necessary' is not on the evaluative lexicon, but the deems/may-deem cue does not require lexicon membership — 'deem' itself makes its object evaluative.
cases.sentence: The board may adopt such bylaws, rules, and regulations as it deems necessary to carry out the purposes of this chapter.

cases.description: Real cue: 'as determined by the department'. The value term ('good cause') is the sentence's own subject, stated well before the cue — this cue has no inline object, so the value term is found by scanning the whole sentence for a lexicon match, not by proximity to the cue.
cases.sentence: Good cause must be found to exist when a person's medical condition, as determined by the department, prevents the person from complying with the reporting requirement.

cases.description: Real cue: 'if it finds that good cause exists'. Inline object ('good cause') gated against the evaluative lexicon so an ordinary factual finding wouldn't be mistaken for delegation; the cue's pronoun actor resolves to the sentence's main actor ('the department').
cases.sentence: The department must grant the petition only if it finds that good cause exists to modify the terms of the order.

cases.description: Real cue: 'as defined by rules of the disciplining authority' — delegated rulemaking. The value term ('cultural competency') is captured directly from the phrase immediately preceding the cue, not gated against the lexicon, since defining a term BY RULEMAKING is itself the delegation regardless of which term is being defined.
cases.sentence: An applicant must demonstrate cultural competency, as defined by rules of the disciplining authority.

cases.description: Must NOT flag as delegated. 'As defined in RCW 69.50.335' is an external reference (a later, separate case), not a delegation to an authority's judgment or rulemaking — distinguishing this from the 'as defined by rules of <authority>' cue above is the point of the guard.
cases.sentence: The department must consider social equity goals as defined in RCW 69.50.335 when awarding licenses.

cases.description: Must NOT flag as delegated. 'Good faith' is a bare evaluative value term with no delegation cue and no named holder anywhere in the sentence — that is the residual/open case, not this one.
cases.sentence: A public agency employee shall not be held liable for any acts or omissions made in good faith under this section.

cases.description: Must NOT flag as delegated. 'Appropriate' is a functional adjective ('suitable/pertinent'), not a contested value term, and there is no delegation cue in the sentence at all.
cases.sentence: The agency must assign appropriate costs to each program based on actual usage.
